Nominatim puts the coordinates on Battubelin, 749 NE 79th St. Infatuation's review and guide (both Feb 2, 2026) confirm it is operating as an outdoor bar 'attached to the back of the Italian restaurant Battubelin, not visible from the street' that uses Battubelin's kitchen. Minor note: category 'speakeasy' is a stretch for a garden patio bar with its own website and press, but that is not a factual claim, so no fix.

Open and correct. The official site lists MiMo, 6910 Biscayne Blvd, open 8am-2pm every day except Tuesday, which matches the windows. Best (08:00) falls inside the hours. Nominatim puts lat/lng exactly at 6910 Biscayne Blvd. Infatuation (Aug 2026) supports the King Guava with guava jam, potato sticks and a fried egg; StarChefs adds cream cheese on a salt bagel. Infatuation also supports 'they sell out a lot (especially on weekends)', mostly takeout, and the Legion Park or Morningside Park picnic idea. One practical problem: Morningside Park is about 1.7 km straight-line from the shop, a 20-25 minute walk, so 'walk it to a bench' undersells the trip. Legion Park, also on the bay, is 0.44 km away. Fix adds the distance and the closer option.

fixes.theMove: Get there at 8am (it sells out, especially weekends) and order the King Guava: cream cheese, guava jam, potato sticks and a fried egg. Take it to a bench in Morningside Park by the bay, about a 25-minute walk or 5-minute drive south. Short on time? Legion Park, also on the bay, is three blocks away. Closed Tuesday.

tasteFlag: Well covered: Infatuation's breakfast guide, Time Out and OAD Cheap Eats all feature it, and the park-picnic pairing comes straight from Infatuation. Still a local favorite rather than a tourist trap.

reason: All checks pass on the Urban Oasis Project page. It lists Legion Park Farmers Market at 6601 Biscayne Blvd, Saturdays 9am-2pm, year-round and rain or shine, which matches the windows and the 09:00 best time. It also confirms 'Free parking in main park lot, 6447 NE 7th Ave', SNAP doubling at all markets, and that SNAP purchases of Florida-grown produce are doubled. Urban Oasis Project is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, and the page names its Florida produce farms. Miami & Beaches confirms Saturday 9-2 at Biscayne Blvd and NE 66th St, run by Urban Oasis, and advises arriving early for parking. Nominatim's reverse result for the lat/lng is the market node itself ('Upper East Side Farmers Market', its former name) on Biscayne Blvd.

Open: the official site has a current music schedule (Fri 10/02, Sat 10/03, Sun 10/04 2026). The site's hours are Sun-Thu 6pm-2am and Fri-Sat 6pm-3am, which match the windows, and it says no reservations. Nominatim puts lat/lng at 3425 NE 2nd Ave. Three corrections: (1) the Infatuation review says the wine is in 'fridges full of wine outside' that you take to the register, not in a fridge inside; (2) music runs every night 9pm-midnight, so a 20:30 arrival is before the band, not 'while the band plays'; (3) the current schedule mixes jazz with blues, soul and Brazilian jazz, so 'live jazz' alone overstates it. Supported as written: mismatched furniture (Infatuation review), string lights (Infatuation best-bars guide, plus the Zagat quote on the official wine page), and packed winter Saturdays (Infatuation, Feb 2026).

fixes.theMove: Go on a weeknight and arrive around 8:30pm to claim one of the mismatched tables under the string lights out back before the 9pm set. Grab a bottle from the self-serve wine fridges, add cheese, pay at the register, and stay while the band plays until midnight. No reservations.
fixes.why: Packed on winter Saturdays, magic on a Tuesday. Still Miami's best backyard wine bar, with live jazz, blues or Brazilian sets every night.

tasteFlag: Mainstream: Infatuation calls it 'Miami's worst-kept secret' and it appears on every best-bars and best-wine-bars list. secret:0 is honest; the weeknight timing is the only insider angle.

reason: Open: the official site lists 295 NW 26th St, Sunday-Friday 7am-5pm, closed Saturday, which matches the windows. Best (07:30) is inside the hours, and Nominatim puts lat/lng at 295 NW 26th St. The FAQ supports the early angle ('two pastry bakes per day, 7am and 12pm'). Kosher status is confirmed by a 2026 certificate. Infatuation (Aug 2026) lists croissants, boureka and babka. Two corrections: (1) the kosher page says it is also closed 'all major Jewish holidays (Rosh Hashana, Yom Kippur, Pesach, Sukkot, & Shavuot)', which matters now since the date falls in the Sukkot/Shemini Atzeret/Simchat Torah window, and 'Closed Saturday' alone is incomplete; (2) the visit page describes a full-service café with table reservations (recommended for weekend mornings), so 'take a table and order from the case' mixes up the two ways to order.

fixes.theMove: Get there around 7:30am, just after the first pastry bake (7am) and before the Wynwood crowd. Pick a croissant, a boureka or a slice of babka from the pastry case, or sit down in the full-service café (walk-ins welcome; book ahead for weekend mornings). Closed Saturdays and major Jewish holidays.

tasteFlag: Mainstream: one of Wynwood's best-known food stops and on every breakfast and bakery guide. secret:0 is honest; going early is the only insider angle.

reason: Open: the Tock page shows 519 NW 26th St and 'Today 7:00 PM - 3:00 AM' on Friday 2026-10-02. Nominatim puts lat/lng at 519 NW 26th St. The windows are wrong: Zona and a Yelp listing updated Sept 2026 both give Tue-Wed and Sun 7pm-2am, Thu-Sat 7pm-3am, closed Monday, but the entry closes every day at 3am. A Fusicology event listing shows Friday closing at 2am, but Tock's own 3am Friday reading outweighs it. Tock confirms both reservation types are 1.5-hour seatings: standard at $25 per person prepaid, and late night at a $50 per person deposit. Tock gives no exact start time for late night, so 'after 10pm' is replaced with 'late-night seating'. Infatuation's best-bars guide (Apr 2026) supports the wasabi peas, cocktails, rotating DJs, record collection and sound system. Time Out supports the Japanese listening-bar lineage. The Haute Living source returned 403 and was not used. Best (23:00) is inside the corrected windows.

fixes.theMove: Book the 90-minute late-night seating on Tock ($50 per person deposit), order a cocktail and wasabi peas, and let the DJ work through the vinyl collection on the hi-fi system. Closed Monday.

tasteFlag: Fairly well known: it is on Infatuation's best-bars list and reviewed by Time Out, so secret:1 overstates it. Still music-first rather than a scene bar, so it fits as a pick.

reason: It's still open. The official Wynwood page lists 2300 NW 2nd Ave, with the restaurant open 11am-2am Mon-Wed and 11am-3am Thu-Sun. Lounge hours are 9pm-2am Mon-Wed and 9pm-3am Thu-Sun. Those match the windows exactly, the 00:30 best time sits inside them, and the claims 'Lounge opens at 9pm' and 'till 3am Thursday to Sunday' are correct. 2026 news covers the brand expanding to Bayside, not the Wynwood original closing. Miami New Times confirms the 'employees only' door into a speakeasy-style bar, and The Infatuation confirms counter ordering and the bar in back. Nominatim puts the pin at 2300 NW 2nd Ave. OSM tags a stale POI name ('Mad Butcher') at the same house number, but the address is right. The one problem is that the same New Times source says most locals and tourist-minded drinkers already know about this door. That contradicts secret: 2, so lower it.
tasteFlag: This is a well-publicized 'hidden' bar. Miami New Times says most locals and tourists already know the employees-only door, and it shows up on every Miami speakeasy listicle. It still works as a late-night move, but it isn't a secret.

reason: The official visit page gives 61 NE 41st St and Wed-Sun 11am-6pm. It's closed Mon, Tue and major federal holidays, and admission is free. The tickets page confirms free timed tickets, and the visit page says advance tickets are 'highly recommended'. The windows (Sun and Wed-Sat, 11:00-18:00) match, and 14:00 is inside them. Nominatim puts the pin on ICA Miami at 61 NE 41st St. 'Closed Monday and Tuesday' is correct. 'Quiet on weekday afternoons' is opinion, not a factual claim. There was an Aug 5-8, 2026 closure, which is past, and I found no fall 2026 closure notice.
tasteFlag: A headline Design District museum (secret: 0) that's in every Miami guide. Free and high quality, but not a non-obvious local pick.

reason: It's open. The official site lists 190 NE 46th St, with hours Tue-Wed 4-10:30pm, Thu-Fri 4-11:30pm, Sat 10am-11:30pm and Sun 10am-10:30pm, closed Monday. That matches the windows exactly. The venue's own music calendar lists the Oct 2 and Oct 3, 2026 sets as 8:00-11:00pm. The Infatuation (Feb 2026) said 'around 8:30pm', but the venue's current calendar is the primary source, so 'music starts around 8:30pm' should become 8pm and best moves to 20:00. 'Live jazz most nights' overclaims. The venue describes nightly concerts of jazz, world, folk, Turkish and Latin music, recent acts were soul and bossa nova, and The Infatuation says 'often jazz'. So soften the title and why. The Infatuation supports the brick dining room, real candles, a bottle of wine for about $60, Resy reservations and the Lagniappe comparison. Nominatim lands on 190 NE 46th St. OSM still shows the prior tenant's name, but the address is right.

fixes.title: Candlelit dinner and live music at Jass Kitchen
fixes.theMove: Book for around 8pm, when live music usually starts (the venue's calendar lists sets from 8 to 11pm, so check it for the night's act), split a bottle of wine, and eat dinner in the brick room by candlelight.
fixes.why: Like a sit-down Lagniappe: real candles, live music most nights (often jazz), and a table you can actually reserve.

tasteFlag: It's getting more press (Cosmopolitan's 50 Best Date Night Spots 2026, an Infatuation guide), but it's still a small neighborhood room that most visitors don't know. Acceptable as a local pick.

reason: The official visit page gives 1100 NW 23rd St and these hours: Wed-Thu and Sun 11:30am-5:30pm, Fri-Sat 11:30am-7:30pm, closed Mon-Tue. That matches the windows exactly, and 15:00 is inside them. The page also confirms 'Complimentary guided tours at 3pm from Wednesday to Sunday' and that the museum is cashless ('Credit or debit cards only; no cash accepted'). Adult admission is $18. The museum's Miami page lists 'Yayoi Kusama' among current exhibitions, and The Fader (Aug 27, 2026) confirms two Kusama Infinity Rooms are on view. Nominatim puts the pin on the museum at 1100 NW 23rd St. One live note: the site says the museum closes early at 5:30pm on Saturday, Oct 3 (tomorrow). That's a one-off and doesn't affect the 3pm tour or the standing windows.
tasteFlag: A major, widely covered museum (secret: 0). The free 3pm tour is a useful tip, but this isn't a non-obvious local pick.

reason: The official Cape Florida Light page says tower tours run 10am-12pm, five days a week, closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays. The park amenities page says Thursday through Monday, and the climb is 109 spiral steps. The windows (Thu-Mon, 10:00-12:00) and the 10:00 best time match. Two things are wrong. First, there is no single '10am tour': tours run throughout 10am to noon. Second, 'free view' is misleading. The climb is free with park entry, but entry costs $8 per vehicle, $4 single occupant, or $2 on foot or bike. The park page confirms it closes when full on busy weekends and holidays. The Miami & Beaches page confirms 'oldest standing structure in Miami-Dade County' and that you can see Stiltsville from the top, so add the word 'standing'. The pin sits on the lighthouse itself (Cape Florida Park Blvd), not at the 1200 S Crandon Blvd park gate. That's more useful for this move, so leave it.

fixes.theMove: Get to the park early (it closes when full on weekends), then join a tower tour (they run 10am to noon, Thursday to Monday) up the 109 steps. Look south from the top for the stilt houses of Stiltsville. Tower closed Tue and Wed.
fixes.why: The oldest standing structure in Miami-Dade, and the best view of Stiltsville without a boat. The climb is free with park entry ($8 per car, $2 on foot or bike).

tasteFlag: A headline state-park attraction that's in every guidebook (secret: 0). The Stiltsville angle and the morning-only tower window add value, but it isn't a non-obvious local pick.

reason: It exists and is open. The official page (lighthouserestaurants.com/the-cleat) gives the same hours as the windows: closed Monday, Tue-Wed 3-8pm, Thu-Fri 3-10pm, Sat 2-10pm, Sun 2-8pm. The address checks out (official: 1200 Crandon Blvd, inside Bill Baggs). The Infatuation best-bars guide (updated Apr 17, 2026) still lists it. 'Tables right on the sand' and the sunset view are supported by Miami New Times (June 2025 piece and Best Waterfront Bar 2022). 'Best waterfront view of any bar in the entire city' is Infatuation's own line. Three things need fixing. (1) lat/lng is exactly the OSM 'No Name Harbor' dock node, which sits in the harbor water. The Google pin for 'The Cleat Mia' (via Wanderlog) is 25.676248,-80.164032, about 130 m away at the harbor mouth. (2) Florida State Parks says the park is open '8 a.m. until sundown' at $8 per vehicle, and the move depends on driving in. The bar's hours to 8 or 10pm overstate drive-in access after dark, so theMove must tell people to get through the gate before sundown. (3) best 18:45 equals '30 min before sunset' only in early October. Computed sunset is 19:07 on Oct 2, 18:40 on Oct 31 and 17:40 from Nov 1, so 18:45 is after dark in November. Use 18:30 for October; it should drop to about 17:10 after Nov 1, or be derived from sunset.

fixes.theMove: Pay the Bill Baggs park entry ($8 per car) and get through the gate before sundown, because the park closes to cars at dusk. Drive to No Name Harbor and take a table on the sand facing the bay about 30 minutes before sunset. Order a cold drink and a snack. Closed Monday.

tasteFlag: Hard to find, but well covered by the press: Infatuation best bars (Apr 2026), New Times Best Waterfront Bar 2022 and Best-Kept Secret 2024. Locals know it, so it is a semi-secret rather than a true insider find. It is not touristy, so it is acceptable.

reason: All checks pass. The schema.org data on the official site says open every day 06:00-15:00, which matches the windows, and best 07:00 falls inside. Nominatim puts lat/lng exactly at 83 Harbor Drive, Key Biscayne. Infatuation's breakfast guide (updated Aug 14, 2026) and its review confirm 'since 1972' and the 'low vinyl stools that overlook a griddle'. They describe the Ted's special as an open-faced sandwich with ham, bacon, tomato, American cheese and two fried eggs on an English muffin, matching theMove. They also say 'the counter's footrest has indented footprints from regulars', which supports the counter-rail footprints. Time Out (2018) also lists 'Daily 6am-3pm'.

The park exists and is open. The official site says 'Open 7:00 am - Sunset, seven days a week (except Thanksgiving and Christmas)' and 'Established in 1945 as a beach for African Americans during segregation', which supports the why. Nominatim resolves lat/lng to Historic Virginia Key Beach Park, 4020 Virginia Beach Dr. best 07:15 is inside the hours. The window's 17:30 close is a conservative stand-in for 'sunset' (about 19:07 today, about 17:30 in December). It never sends anyone to a closed park, so it is not blocking. The issue is the sunrise claim. Computed Miami sunrise is 07:12-07:27 in October, so 'walk to the water as the sun comes up' after the 7am opening works then. From Nov 1 to about Dec 21, sunrise is 06:28-07:02, so the sun is already up before the gate opens, and the claim is false for most of fall. Reworded below. Also note: on Monday Oct 12, 2026, 8am-2pm, a ticketed Carnival fete (Stink and Dutty) takes over the park, so skip that morning. The park was also closed Jan 26-Feb 12, 2026 for events, which shows event closures happen.

fixes.theMove: Be at the gate when it opens at 7am and walk straight to the water. In October the sun rises over the Atlantic just after opening; from November it is already up, so you get the first quiet hour of light instead. Swim before the heat sets in.

reason: Hours, tours and address check out. The official plan-your-visit page says '10 AM - 5 PM (no admission after 4 PM)', open daily except Thanksgiving and Christmas. It lists the Guided Museum Tour daily at 11:30am and Nature Preserve Tours 'daily at 12:30 PM, October - May', both included with admission, and the Mangrove Boardwalk open 10-5. Address is 16701 SW 72 Ave, Palmetto Bay; Nominatim resolves lat/lng to that address; best 10:00 is inside the hours. Three fixes. (1) 'national landmark' is wrong. The estate is on the National Register of Historic Places (ref 86000325, 1986) and is not a designated National Historic Landmark. (2) No source confirms the boardwalk reaches the bay. Official and secondary sources only say it runs through the mangrove forest, so 'to the bay' is removed. (3) The Stone House, the main historic building, has been closed for renovation since April 28, 2025. The 11:30 tour still runs per the official page, but visitors should know. Wikipedia supports the hardwood hammock.

fixes.theMove: Arrive at 10am and walk the mangrove boardwalk, then take the 11:30 museum tour (the Stone House is closed for restoration) and the 12:30 nature preserve tour (October to May). Both tours are included with admission. Last entry is 4pm.
fixes.why: A historic bayfront estate on the National Register of Historic Places, with tropical hardwood hammock and mangroves. Old Miami, far from the crowds.

tasteFlag: A well-known, ticketed county attraction (secret 0). It is a solid local staple but not a non-obvious pick.

reason: The live official site (fetched today, Oct 2, 2026) says 'Open everyday from 9am-6pm. We are closed Thanksgiving and Christmas Day', with the address 19200 SW 344th St, Homestead. That matches the windows, and best 10:00 is inside. The site advertises fresh-fruit shakes ('Hand-cut fruit, blended to perfection. Our shakes and smoothies are iconic') and in-season tropical fruit, which supports theMove. Nominatim puts lat/lng at 19200 SW 344th St. One real open question: Art of Eating (Feb 2024) says the owner 'now shuts down in September and October'. The current official site lists no seasonal closure, and search excerpts I did not open (a Facebook 'Happy October... open everyday' post, TripAdvisor and Yelp hours, Farm Hop pickup days Oct 1-4, 2026) suggest it is open now. The live primary source wins. The Instagram bio (search excerpt) says weekends open at 8am, and the 9am windows sit inside that.
tasteFlag: Mainstream. It is the best-known roadside stop on the road to the Everglades and Keys, with TripAdvisor reviewers calling it a 'tourist magnet' and coverage from Food Network, NBC and Fox. Wanderlog ranks it #3 of things to do in Homestead. Worth doing, but it is not an insider pick.

reason: Open and current: the official Florida State Parks pages (main page dated 2026-10-01) give Thursday to Monday, 9am to 5pm, closed Tuesday, Wednesday, Christmas and New Year's Day. That matches days [0,1,4,5,6], assuming 0 = Sunday, which is the only reading where 'closed Tue/Wed' works and is consistent across all three entries. House tours run at 10am, 11:30am, 1pm and 2:30pm, so best 10:00 is inside hours. The address 3485 Main Hwy is correct. Built in 1891 on Biscayne Bay is confirmed by thebarnacle.org. The lawn-to-bay view is confirmed by TCLF ('wide views of the bay across an expanse of lawn'). Two problems. (1) '$2 at the gate' merges two fees. $2 is day-use entry only: exact change in the honor box, at the Carriage House Gift Shop, or online. The official page says admission does not cover the house interior. The tour is a separate $3 ticket (ages 13+) from the gift shop, capped at 10 people. (2) The lat/lng is outside the park. It reverse-geocodes to 3498 Main Hwy, about 45m west of the park boundary on the Coconut Grove Playhouse side of the street. A point-in-polygon test against the OSM park outline says it is outside. The OSM 3485 address node (25.726466,-80.244197) is also just outside and reverse-geocodes to 3484. The corrected point 25.7263,-80.24395 is inside the park outline at the Main Hwy frontage (reverse: Commodore Trail). I added getIn from the official fee page: no vehicle entry, metered street parking.

fixes.theMove: Pay the $2 entry (exact change in the honor box, or at the Carriage House gift shop), then buy a $3 ticket there for the 10am house tour. Tours cap at 10 people, so arrive a little before. Afterward, walk the lawn down to the bayfront. Closed Tuesday and Wednesday.
fixes.getIn: Walk or bike in from Main Highway; no cars inside the park, so use the metered street parking nearby.

reason: Open as of fall 2026: the official Instagram @maesinthegrove posted Sept 9, Sept 29 and Oct 1, 2026, and its bio reads 'Monday–Saturday starting at 5PM'. The official site maesmiami.com gives Mon–Wed 5PM–1AM, Thu–Sat 5PM–2AM, Sunday closed, walk-ins only, happy hour Mon–Sat 5–7PM with $9 cocktails. The data's 2:00/3:00 closing times come from the coconutgrove.com listing, which conflicts with the official site. I went with the official site. The address (3444 Main Hwy Ste 17) and coordinates (the OSM node at 3444 Main Hwy) are fine. Confirmed claims: 'courtyard behind Chug's Diner' (Miami New Times 2025; Herald article via AOL); seat-only with no standing room and martinis served frost-bitten from the freezer (Infatuation Best Bars, July 2026, and Infatuation review). Wrong claims: the food does not come from Chug's Diner. It comes from Chuggie's (Suite 15), ordered by scanning the QR code on the back of Mae's menu (IG post of Sept 29, 2026). 'The O.G.' is on Chuggie's menu. Chuggie's kitchen closes at 10pm Sun–Wed and 11pm Thu–Sat, so best 22:30 would leave no burger Mon–Wed. I moved best to 18:30. That is inside happy hour, early enough to get a seat (Infatuation says get there early), and Chuggie's is open. I also added the kitchen cutoff to theMove. In why, 'you always get a seat' overstates it, since you may wait outside. I reworded it. Sources should add maesmiami.com, the Chuggie's menu and the Sept 29 IG post.

fixes.theMove: Find the courtyard behind Chug's Diner. There's no standing room, so come early (happy hour is 5 to 7pm with $9 cocktails) or wait for a seat. Order a cold martini, then scan the QR code on the back of the menu to get Chuggie's O.G. burger sent over from next door. Chuggie's kitchen closes at 10pm Monday to Wednesday and 11pm Thursday to Saturday. Walk-ins only. Closed Sunday.
fixes.why: A tiny cocktail den in a Grove courtyard where everyone inside has a seat and nobody steps on your shoes.

tasteFlag: Not really secret. It is on The Infatuation's current Best Bars in Miami list (8.2) and has had Herald, Axios and New Times coverage since opening. It is still a neighborhood cocktail bar rather than a tourist spot, but secret:1 is generous.

reason: Open: the official site (katanamiamibeach.com now redirects to katanajapaneserestaurant.com) gives 'Open Everyday 6PM - 12AM, last call 11:30PM' and an average wait of 45–60 minutes. The contact page says 'No reservations', about 30 seats, and parties of 5+ go to sister restaurant Shima. Windows and best 18:00 are correct. The address 920 71st St is right, and the coordinates match the OSM 'Katana' node exactly, placed on the Isle of Normandy, which confirms 'Normandy Isle'. Three claims are stale, coming from a 2022 Infatuation review. (1) The take-a-ticket, listen-for-your-number system: Miami New Times (2026) says you put your name down, leave your phone number, and get a call, with about five minutes to claim the seat before it goes to the next person. (2) 'Arrive right at 6pm': New Times advises arriving 30 minutes before opening to make the first seating. Best stays 18:00 because it must sit inside the open hours. (3) 'Plates start at $1.50': New Times 2026 says dishes start around $2.90 (tamago or shrimp) and go up to about $12 (uni), priced by plate color. Also, the spots-of-summer-miami source covers Katana Coral Way, a different location, so I replaced it.

fixes.theMove: Get there around 5:30pm, before the 6pm opening, and put your name and phone number on the list. When they call, you have about five minutes to claim your seat or it goes to the next person. Then pull plates off the little boats; price goes by plate color, from about $2.90 (tamago, shrimp) up to about $12 (uni).

tasteFlag: An institution, not a secret. New Times (2026) says practically everyone knows about it and the wait can hit two hours, and The Infatuation calls it everyone's favorite sushi-boat spot (there is now a second location on Coral Way). It is a genuine locals' place and not touristy, but secret:1 overstates it.
